name: Oscar Guzman
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember swapping holiday sweaters with my twin.” On Friday, near the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, Oscar can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I carried a debt for my brother because the old man never knew which twin was which.
appearance: Oscar has a long plait tucked inside the collar, a straight nose and deep-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. When somebody else has the floor, Oscar folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Oscar is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To clear up which twin incurred the debt.
family: Asa Roberts is Oscar’s cousin. Oscar can stop the walk at any corner. Asa chooses the familiar route. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *Closing soup*, Asa says, “I want the recipe credited to the people who chop after their shift ends.”
connections: Loretta Banks. A rent envelope helps separate one twin's debt from the other's.

reactions.situation: The former fence offers to pay money for something irreplaceable
reactions.response: Oscar asks the owner what returning money would and wouldn't settle.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Oscar asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.

reactions.situation: When everyone else wants to celebrate immediately
reactions.response: Oscar helps set the table, then takes a short turn outside alone.
